title: Local intersection and localization data for an affine SNC root presentation
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring such that $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ is regular [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Let $I$ be a finite index set, and let $t_i\in A$ for $i\in I$ cut out precisely the pairwise distinct reduced irreducible branches, as closed subschemes $V(t_i)$, of a strict normal crossings boundary on $X$ [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary]. For an integer $n\geq1$ put $C=A[x_i:i\in I]/(x_i^n-t_i:i\in I)$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Then $A$ and $C$ are Noetherian. For every prime $p\subset A$, put $R=A_p$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], let $\mathfrak m=pA_p$, write $\bar t_i=t_i/1$, and set $S=\{i\in I:t_i\in p\}$. For every $J\subseteq S$, the ring $R_J=R/(\bar t_j:j\in J)$ is regular local, and $\dim R_J+|J|=\dim R$, where dimension is Krull dimension [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Every $\bar t_i$ with $i\notin S$ is a unit in $R$ and in every $R_J$. There is a canonical isomorphism $(A\setminus p)^{-1}C\cong R[x_i:i\in I]/(x_i^n-\bar t_i:i\in I)$ sending coefficients to their fractions and each root coordinate to the coordinate with the same index. For every prime $q\subset C$ contracting to $p$, if $Q$ is its extension to the ring on the right, this isomorphism induces an isomorphism of that ring localized at $Q$ with $C_q$, fixing the image of $C$. No regularity of $C$ is asserted. Zero rings and empty index sets are allowed; the prime-indexed assertions are vacuous when $A=0$.

source.place: Tag 0BIA (lemma-strict-normal-crossings), regular-intersection criterion and proof; applied to the full parameter-root presentation of ILO Expose IX Proposition 2.1, printed p.133. The coefficient and quotient localization identifications and affine Noetherianity are those of the original item steps 1, 2 and 7.

proof.text: Regularity of $X$ implies that $X$ is locally Noetherian. Apply the affine-open Noetherianity lemma to the affine open $X$ itself to obtain that $A$ is Noetherian. Choose an enumeration of the finite set $I$. The displayed presentation of $C$ is then a quotient of a polynomial ring in $|I|$ variables over $A$, so the finite-type algebra Noetherianity lemma gives that $C$ is Noetherian. This also applies to $I=\varnothing$ and to the zero ring.

Fix p and J. The integral subschemes in the SNC definition have irreducible closed supports covering H. Each actual irreducible component of H lies in one of this finite family of supports, hence equals it by maximality. Choose these indices: distinct actual components give distinct indices, so the resulting map Fin r into the SNC index set is injective. The selected subschemes and the principal prime quotient spectra have the same supports and are reduced; their ideal sheaves are therefore equal. Their intersection D has global ideal K_J=(t_j:j in J), by the supremum formula for ideal sheaves and the affine quotient kernel formula. Since K_J is contained in p, the point x of Spec A corresponding to p lifts to z in D. The map from the stalk of Spec A at x to the stalk of D at z is surjective. Its kernel is the extension of K_J, by Scheme.Hom.ker_stalkMap. Transport across Spec.stalkIso and take the first isomorphism theorem to obtain A_p/K_J A_p isomorphic to the stalk of D at z. The SNC intersection condition now gives regularity and the dimension equality, and injectivity of the chosen indices preserves |J|. This also handles empty J.

source.place: Tag 0BIA (lemma-strict-normal-crossings), regular-intersection criterion; Schemes Tag 01HV (lemma-spec-sheaves)(6); Algebra Tag 00CT (proposition-localize-quotient).

proof.text: If $i\notin S$, then $t_i\notin p$, so $1/t_i$ is a fraction in $R=A_p$ and $(t_i/1)(1/t_i)=1$. Applying the quotient map $R\to R_J$ to this equality gives an inverse for the image of $\bar t_i$ in every $R_J$. No property of $n$ is used here.

Put R=A_p, P=A[x_i], S=R[x_i], and let I and J be the respective root relation ideals. The coefficient extension P to S maps I exactly to J, by Ideal.map_span and the formulas for mapping X and C. MvPolynomial.isLocalization identifies S as the localization of P at the images of A minus p. IsLocalization.of_surjective then identifies S/(I S) as the localization of P/I at the images of these denominators. Transport this localization structure across the quotient equivalence given by I S=J. Thus B=S/J is a localization of C=P/I at exactly the same multiplicative subset as the displayed Localization.

source.place: Tag 00CP (proposition-universal-property-localization), proof by the explicit fraction formula; polynomial evaluation and quotient relations.

proof.text: Apply IsLocalization.algEquiv to the two localizations of C to obtain the required ring equivalence e. Its coefficient and coordinate formulas follow from AlgEquiv.commutes and the formulas for the polynomial quotient map. For uniqueness, two such equivalences agree after precomposition with C by quotient surjectivity and MvPolynomial.ringHom_ext: their values on coefficients and variables agree. IsLocalization.ringHom_ext then gives equality on the localization.

source.place: Tag 00CP (proposition-universal-property-localization), explicit inverse and uniqueness calculation; Tag 00CT (proposition-localize-quotient), quotient-map construction.

proof.text: For a prime q of C contracting to p, its intersection with the image of A minus p is empty. Give B its C-algebra structure through e. Transport the localization instance along e and apply IsLocalization.isPrime_of_isPrime_disjoint to see that Q=qB is prime. The contraction equality Q intersect C=q is IsLocalization.under_map_of_isPrime_disjoint.

source.place: Tag 00E3 (lemma-spec-localization), numerator proof of prime extension, written out using Tag 00CO fractions.

proof.text: The localization of B at Q is a localization of C at q, by IsLocalization.isLocalization_isLocalization_atPrime_isLocalization and the contraction equality. Apply IsLocalization.algEquiv with C_q. AlgEquiv.commutes proves that the resulting equivalence fixes every element of C. All constructions are valid for empty branch sets and n=1. If A is the zero ring, there are no primes p, so its prime-indexed conclusions are vacuous.

e : Localization (p.primeCompl.map (algebraMap A ((MvPolynomial (Fin r) A ⧸ Ideal.span (Set.range (fun i : Fin r ↦ MvPolynomial.X i ^ n - MvPolynomial.C (t i))))))) ≃+* (MvPolynomial (Fin r) (Localization.AtPrime p) ⧸ Ideal.span (Set.range (fun i : Fin r ↦ MvPolynomial.X i ^ n - MvPolynomial.C (algebraMap A (Localization.AtPrime p) (t i))))), (∀ a : A, e (algebraMap ((MvPolynomial (Fin r) A ⧸ Ideal.span (Set.range (fun i : Fin r ↦ MvPolynomial.X i ^ n - MvPolynomial.C (t i))))) _ (algebraMap A ((MvPolynomial (Fin r) A ⧸ Ideal.span (Set.range (fun i : Fin r ↦ MvPolynomial.X i ^ n - MvPolynomial.C (t i))))) a)) = algebraMap (Localization.AtPrime p) _ (algebraMap A (Localization.AtPrime p) a)) ∧ (∀ i : Fin r, e (algebraMap ((MvPolynomial (Fin r) A ⧸ Ideal.span (Set.range (fun i : Fin r ↦ MvPolynomial.X i ^ n - MvPolynomial.C (t i))))) _ (Ideal.Quotient.mk _ (MvPolynomial.X i))) = Ideal.Quotient.mk _ (MvPolynomial.X i)) ∧ ∀ (q : Ideal ((MvPolynomial (Fin r) A ⧸ Ideal.span (Set.range (fun i : Fin r ↦ MvPolynomial.X i ^ n - MvPolynomial.C (t i)))))) [q.IsPrime], q.comap (algebraMap A ((MvPolynomial (Fin r) A ⧸ Ideal.span (Set.range (fun i : Fin r ↦ MvPolynomial.X i ^ n - MvPolynomial.C (t i)))))) = p → ∃ (Q : Ideal ((MvPolynomial (Fin r) (Localization.AtPrime p) ⧸ Ideal.span (Set.range (fun i : Fin r ↦ MvPolynomial.X i ^ n - MvPolynomial.C (algebraMap A (Localization.AtPrime p) (t i))))))) (_hQ : Q.IsPrime), Q = q.map (e.toRingHom.comp (algebraMap ((MvPolynomial (Fin r) A ⧸ Ideal.span (Set.range (fun i : Fin r ↦ MvPolynomial.X i ^ n - MvPolynomial.C (t i))))) _)) ∧ ∃ eq : Localization.AtPrime Q ≃+* Localization.AtPrime q, ∀ c : (MvPolynomial (Fin r) A ⧸ Ideal.span (Set.range (fun i : Fin r ↦ MvPolynomial.X i ^ n - MvPolynomial.C (t i)))), eq (Localization.mk (e (Localization.mk c 1)) 1) = Localization.mk c 1
